title: Improving the consistency of multitemporal land cover maps using a hidden Markov model
source: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing 54(2), 703-713
relevance: Applies an HMM as post-processing to a classification time series, using transition and emission probabilities to separate real land cover change from classification error - the standard fix for the unrealistically high year-to-year label churn that multitemporal products exhibit. Directly applicable to our flicker problem, and the transition matrix is where our domain knowledge would enter (canopy rarely appears or vanishes in one year). But note the hazard for THIS project: the same prior that suppresses spurious transitions also suppresses genuine rapid canopy LOSS, which is the policy-relevant signal a tree ordinance is about. Adopt it only with the transition prior stated and its effect on real loss events measured.

title: Time-series land cover change detection using deep learning-based temporal semantic segmentation
relevance: Learns land cover change by segmenting the TEMPORAL dimension directly rather than differencing independently classified dates, which is the model-side answer to the false-change problem our Search 42 found on the human-interpretation side. Relevant because our pipeline currently produces per-year masks independently and infers change by comparison, so every per-year error becomes a candidate change event. Also note the accompanying finding that temporal-consistency losses do NOT require ground-truth labels - which would let all 17 unlabelled years contribute to training, an asset we currently use only for inference.
